cases.steps: Save as draft. Search the events list for the title.
cases.expected: One row, status Draft. No vendor can see it.
cases.oracle: Status is draft; as an invited-vendor-to-be, the event is absent from the portal.

cases.title: Save as draft is available before the event is valid
cases.why: The point of a draft is to save work that is not yet publishable. If draft ran the publish validations it would be useless.
cases.setup: A project with a title only.
cases.steps: Save as draft.
cases.expected: Saved, with no validation errors about sheet, schedule or participants.
cases.oracle: Draft created; no error toast.

cases.title: The confirm modal states the invited vendor count
cases.why: "Vendors invited: 0" in that modal is the last chance to catch an audience that never populated — and it is easy to click straight past.
cases.setup: An event with a known number of participants.
cases.steps: Press Publish and read the modal.
cases.expected: The count matches the participants actually selected.
cases.oracle: Modal count == participant count; fail if 0 when participants were selected.

cases.title: Cancelling the confirm modal publishes nothing
cases.why: A cancel that half-commits is the worst possible outcome at this step.
cases.setup: A valid event.
cases.steps: Press Publish, then cancel the modal.
cases.expected: Still on the create screen; no event with that title exists as Live.
cases.oracle: URL unchanged; zero Live rows for the title.

cases.title: Double-clicking Publish creates one event, not two
cases.why: A slow publish invites a second click, and two events with one title breaks every find-by-title oracle after it.
cases.setup: A valid event.
cases.steps: Click Publish twice quickly, confirm.
cases.expected: One event.
cases.oracle: Exactly one row for the title in the events list.

cases.title: Publishing a two-stage event orders the stages correctly
cases.why: `STANDARD_STAGES_SEQUENCE` is `{rfp: 1, rfq: 2, auction: 3, rfq_then_auction: 4}`, and out-of-order stages would let vendors price before they qualify.
cases.setup: An RFP + RFQ event.
cases.steps: Publish. Read the stage order on the project.
cases.expected: RFP first, RFQ second, regardless of the order the tabs were built in.
cases.oracle: Stage sequence numbers ascend in that order.

cases.title: A stage left out of the publish selection is voided, not published
cases.why: Only the stages named in the publish request go live; any other stage on the event group is voided. A stage that survives as a ghost would accept bids nobody expects.
cases.setup: A project with three draft stages, two selected for publish.
cases.steps: Publish the two.
cases.expected: Two live stages; the third is voided and invisible.
cases.oracle: Stage count on the live event = 2. Pairs with API-PUB-024.

cases.title: Publish is refused for a user without trade create permission
cases.why: Publishing is the privileged action in this module, and the gate is a team-based permission rather than a role name.
cases.setup: A user in a team without `trade: create_record`.
cases.steps: Try to reach the create screen and publish.
cases.expected: Either the entry point is absent or the publish is refused with "You are not allowed to perform this action".
cases.oracle: No event created; a readable refusal.

cases.title: Publish on a superseded version of the event is refused
cases.why: Two tabs on one draft is a real scenario, and publishing the stale one would silently discard the newer work.
cases.setup: A draft opened in two tabs; publish from tab 1, then from tab 2.
cases.steps: Publish from the older tab.
cases.expected: Refused because that version is not the latest.
cases.oracle: Error code 101 / "not allowed"; the event reflects tab 1's publish only.

cases.title: An approval-required event goes to Requested, not Live
cases.why: On tenants with publish approvals, "published" means "awaiting approval", and a test asserting Live would fail forever on those tenants.
cases.setup: gate: publish approval configured.
cases.steps: Publish.
cases.expected: The stage status is Requested and an approval task exists.
cases.oracle: Status Requested; the approver sees a pending task.

cases.title: Auto-routing to the auction team leaves the stage in Draft
cases.why: gate: `routeAuctionsToAuctionTeam`. The publish appears not to have worked, and this case is where that expectation is written down.
cases.setup: gate: `routeAuctionsToAuctionTeam`. An auction stage.
cases.steps: Publish.
cases.expected: The stage is handed to the auction team and stays Draft for the publisher.
cases.oracle: Status draft plus an auction-team assignment — not an error.

cases.title: Publishing sends invitations to every invited vendor
cases.why: PRD §3.3's audience promise is only real if the invitation lands.
cases.setup: An event with two invited vendors.
cases.steps: Publish. Check each vendor's portal list and mailbox.
cases.expected: Both see the event; both receive an invitation.
cases.oracle: Portal listing is the automatable half; mail delivery is manual.

cases.title: The published event carries a reference id
cases.why: `RFX-…` at project level and per-stage ids are how humans talk about events; a missing one makes support impossible.
cases.setup: A published event.
cases.steps: Read the ids on the project and each stage.
cases.expected: A project ref id and a per-stage ref id, both non-empty and unique.
cases.oracle: Ids present and matching the events-list row.

cases.title: Republishing an already-live event is idempotent
cases.why: A retry after a timeout must not duplicate stages or audiences.
cases.setup: A live event.
cases.steps: Re-issue the publish action.
cases.expected: Nothing changes.
cases.oracle: Stage count, audience count and bid count all unchanged. Pairs with API-PUB-025.

cases.title: Withdrawing a live event requires a remark and closes it to vendors
cases.why: Withdrawal is the buyer's emergency stop; without the remark requirement there is no audit trail.
cases.setup: A live event with an invited vendor.
cases.steps: Withdraw with an empty remark, then with a real one.
cases.expected: First refused; second withdraws the event and the vendor can no longer bid.
cases.oracle: Status withdrawn; as the vendor, bidding is refused ("Order not active").

cases.title: A withdrawn event cannot be re-activated
cases.why: Resurrecting a withdrawn event would reopen bidding vendors were told was over.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event.
cases.steps: Try to publish/activate it again.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Status stays withdrawn. Pairs with API-LC-005.

cases.title: Withdrawing twice does not duplicate the remark or the notification
cases.why: Idempotency on the emergency stop, and vendors receiving two withdrawal mails is a support call.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event.
cases.steps: Withdraw again.
cases.expected: No second remark, no second notification.
cases.oracle: One withdrawal record.

cases.title: An active event can be cloned
cases.why: Cloning is how buyers run the same event monthly, and its policy has four separate refusal conditions worth pinning.
cases.setup: An active event, not created from a PR, buyer not a planner.
cases.steps: Clone it.
cases.expected: A new draft with the same line items, template and configuration, and its own ref id.
cases.oracle: New draft exists; line items and template match; the ref id differs.

cases.title: Cloning a draft is refused
cases.why: One of the four refusals, and the least intuitive.
cases.setup: A draft event.
cases.steps: Try to clone.
cases.expected: Refused ("Only active or withdrawn events can be cloned.").
cases.oracle: Message shown; no clone created.

cases.title: Cloning a PR-created event is refused
cases.why: The clone would have no requisition behind it.
cases.setup: An event created from a PR.
cases.steps: Try to clone.
cases.expected: Refused ("Events with purchase requests cannot be cloned.").
cases.oracle: Message shown.

cases.title: Amending a published event requires amendment remarks
cases.why: An amendment changes the terms vendors bid against; the remark is what they are shown.
cases.setup: A published event, amendment started.
cases.steps: Publish the amendment with blank remarks, then with real ones.
cases.expected: First refused; second published and vendors notified.
cases.oracle: Amendment recorded with the remark text.

cases.title: Changing ownership of an event works for the owner and not for others
cases.why: It is how an event survives someone leaving, and it is permission-sensitive (owner, super-admin or Procol employee only).
cases.setup: An event, its owner, and an unrelated buyer.
cases.steps: Change ownership as the owner; then attempt it as the unrelated buyer.
cases.expected: The first succeeds; the second is refused.
cases.oracle: New owner reflected; refusal on the second attempt.

cases.title: Convert to Auction is offered on a published RFQ
cases.why: The entry point is behind the event Settings menu and is gated three ways: published (not draft), vendor masking off, and the tenant allowing it.
cases.setup: A published RFQ; vendor masking off.
cases.steps: Open the event → Settings (`event-settings-button`) → read the menu.
cases.expected: "Convert to Auction" is listed.
cases.oracle: The item exists. If Settings opens and simply does not list it, report that the feature is gated off on this tenant — not that the automation is wrong.

cases.title: Conversion opens a prefilled create screen in a new tab
cases.why: It `window.open`s with `isRfqToAuction=true&draftStageIds=…`; a test driving the original tab watches a page that never changes.
cases.steps: Settings → Convert to Auction → Continue.
cases.expected: A new tab on the create screen with the conversion query params, the RFQ's template and sheet already in place.
cases.oracle: Handle the new page object; assert `isRfqToAuction=true` in its URL.

cases.title: The converted auction publishes with the RFQ's data
cases.why: The whole point: carry the RFQ's quotes and participants into an auction without re-entering anything.
cases.steps: On the conversion screen, invite vendors and publish.
cases.expected: An auction event linked to the RFQ, with the same line items.
cases.oracle: Redirect to a project id; no error toast; line items match the RFQ's.

cases.title: The template picker is locked during conversion
cases.why: Changing the schema would invalidate the carried-over quotes.
cases.setup: A conversion screen.
cases.steps: Try to open the template dropdown.
cases.expected: Disabled.
cases.oracle: Dropdown disabled.

cases.title: "All invited" carries every RFQ participant, not just the bidders
cases.why: The toggle switches the audience source, and the difference decides who can bid in the auction.
cases.setup: An RFQ where 2 of 5 invited vendors bid.
cases.steps: Convert with the toggle off, then (on a second conversion) with it on.
cases.expected: Off: only the 2 bidders carry forward as bidding participants. On: all 5 carry, with the bidders flagged.
cases.oracle: Participant counts 2 and 5 respectively; the bid-placed flag set on the right ones.

cases.title: TNA vendors are included or excluded per the flag
cases.why: gate: `allowTnaVendorsToBid`. Getting it wrong either bars legitimate bidders or admits ones who should not bid.
cases.setup: An RFQ audience containing TNA vendors.
cases.steps: Convert with the flag off, then on.
cases.expected: Excluded when off, included when on.
cases.oracle: The TNA vendor's presence in the bidding audience flips with the flag.

cases.title: Converting the same RFQ twice is refused
cases.why: The model enforces at most one non-cancelled auction per parent RFQ, so the second attempt must be refused rather than creating an orphan.
cases.setup: An already-converted RFQ.
cases.steps: Try to convert again.
cases.expected: Refused ("An auction has already been made for this trade.").
cases.oracle: Message shown; still exactly one auction child.

cases.title: The RFQ becomes uneditable once its auction exists
cases.why: The backend refuses RFQ edits after conversion ("You cannot edit rfq once the auction is created.", 769) and the UI must not offer them.
cases.setup: A converted RFQ.
cases.steps: Try to edit the RFQ's sheet or schedule.
cases.expected: Refused or unavailable.
cases.oracle: No successful edit; a readable refusal if attempted.

cases.title: Convert to Auction is hidden when vendor masking is on
cases.why: Masking and conversion are incompatible, and the control's visibility is the whole enforcement.
cases.setup: gate: `isVendorMaskingEnabled`. A published RFQ.
cases.steps: Open Settings.
cases.expected: No Convert to Auction item, regardless of the RFQ's state.
cases.oracle: Item absent.

cases.title: Conversion on a draft RFQ is not offered
cases.why: There are no quotes to carry from a draft, so the control must not appear.
cases.setup: A draft RFQ.
cases.steps: Open Settings.
cases.expected: Not offered.
cases.oracle: Item absent.

cases.title: Conversion is refused on a superseded event version
cases.why: Same staleness problem as UI-PUB-011, on a path that creates a new trade record.
cases.setup: An RFQ whose event group has a newer version.
cases.steps: Attempt the conversion.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No auction created.

cases.title: Fast bidding needs more than one line item
cases.why: The backend refuses with a specific message ("CBD mode requires at least two active line items."), which is only meaningful if the UI surfaces it.
cases.setup: gate: fast bidding. A single-line-item RFQ.
cases.steps: Convert with fast bidding on.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: Message shown; no auction created.

cases.title: Vendors carried into the auction can bid immediately
cases.why: The conversion is only useful if the carried audience can act, and audience-carry bugs show up here first.
cases.setup: A converted auction, live.
cases.steps: As a carried-over vendor, open the auction and bid.
cases.expected: The bid is accepted.
cases.oracle: Bid submitted; visible to the buyer on the auction.

cases.title: The RFQ's bids remain visible after conversion
cases.why: The RFQ's history is the baseline the auction's savings are measured against.
cases.setup: A converted RFQ that had bids.
cases.steps: Open the RFQ stage on the project.
cases.expected: Its bids are still there, read-only.
cases.oracle: Bid count on the RFQ unchanged after conversion.

cases.title: A BOQ project creates its draft event group exactly once on mount
cases.why: A re-render that fires it again produces two draft events and the buyer works in one while the other lingers.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed`.
cases.steps: Enter BOQ project creation. Let the screen re-render (resize, switch tabs).
cases.expected: One draft event group.
cases.oracle: Exactly one create request; one draft in the events list.

cases.title: A BOQ event is accepted with no line items in the create request
cases.why: It is the one legal way to create an event with an empty `line_items` array — the flag is what makes it legal.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed`.
cases.steps: Create the BOQ draft before uploading anything.
cases.expected: Created.
cases.oracle: Draft created with zero line items. Pairs with API-EG-004.

cases.title: BOQ creation is refused on a tenant that does not allow it
cases.why: The negative half of the gate; without it the flag is unproven.
cases.setup: A tenant without `boq_in_erfx_allowed`.
cases.steps: Attempt BOQ creation.
cases.expected: Refused ("You are not allowed to perform this action") or the entry point absent.
cases.oracle: No draft created. Pairs with API-EG-005.

cases.title: Downloading the blank BOQ template gives a usable sheet
cases.why: It is the buyer's starting point; a template whose columns do not match the importer is an immediate dead end.
cases.setup: A BOQ project with a template chosen.
cases.steps: Download the blank BOQ items sheet.
cases.expected: A spreadsheet whose columns match the chosen template's schema.
cases.oracle: Column headers equal the template's widget names.

cases.title: Uploading a filled BOQ sheet creates one line item per row
cases.why: It is the core BOQ mechanic and the only bulk line-item path.
cases.setup: A filled sheet with 25 rows.
cases.steps: Upload it.
cases.expected: 25 line items, values as in the sheet.
cases.oracle: Badge = 25; spot-check three rows' product, quantity and unit.

cases.title: A malformed BOQ row is reported with its row number
cases.why: "Upload failed" on a 500-row sheet is useless; the row number is the whole value of the error.
cases.setup: A sheet with a bad quantity on row 12.
cases.steps: Upload.
cases.expected: A readable error naming row 12; either nothing imports or the good rows import and the bad one is listed.
cases.oracle: The message contains the row identifier; no 500.

cases.title: A BOQ upload with a product that does not exist is refused
cases.why: The backend answers "Product not found" (80) and the buyer needs to know which product.
cases.setup: A sheet naming an unknown product.
cases.steps: Upload.
cases.expected: Refused, naming the offending value.
cases.oracle: Message identifies the product; no partial import of that row.

cases.title: Re-uploading replaces the previous BOQ items
cases.why: Appending instead of replacing silently doubles a 500-row event.
cases.setup: A BOQ event with 25 items.
cases.steps: Upload a different 25-row sheet.
cases.expected: 25 items, the new ones; the old ones are removed.
cases.oracle: Count is 25, not 50; the old products are gone. Pairs with API-LI-007.

cases.title: 500 BOQ items publish
cases.why: The documented ceiling, and the only case that exercises the publish path at scale.
cases.setup: gate: `boq_in_erfx_allowed`.
cases.steps: Load 500 items. Publish.
cases.expected: Publishes.
cases.oracle: Publish succeeds; record the duration (see UI-NFR-004).

cases.title: 501 BOQ items are refused
cases.why: The other side of the boundary.
cases.steps: Attempt 501.
cases.expected: Refused with the max-line-items message.
cases.oracle: Message shown; the event keeps 500.

cases.title: A vendor bidding on a BOQ event gets all rows in their sheet
cases.why: A truncated vendor sheet produces a partial bid that looks complete.
cases.setup: A live BOQ event with 25 items and an invited vendor.
cases.steps: As the vendor, open the bid sheet.
cases.expected: 25 rows, matching the buyer's items.
cases.oracle: Row count and the products in each row match.

cases.title: A BOQ event linked to a purchase request validates the PR
cases.why: `purchase_request_id` must resolve to an active BOQ PR owned by the workspace, or the event is attached to nothing.
cases.setup: A BOQ project and an inactive/foreign PR id.
cases.steps: Attempt to link it.
cases.expected: Refused ("not allowed").
cases.oracle: No link created. Pairs with API-PUB-016.

cases.title: An approved PR converts into a draft event
cases.why: It is the intake-to-sourcing handoff, and everything about the resulting event is constrained by it.
cases.setup: gate: PR module. An approved PR with line items.
cases.steps: From the PR, create an event.
cases.expected: A draft event carrying the PR's line items and quantities.
cases.oracle: Line-item count and products match the PR; the event records the PR link.

cases.title: PR line items cannot be added to or removed
cases.why: Diverging from the requisition breaks the consumption reconciliation.
cases.setup: A PR-created draft.
cases.steps: Open the line-items drawer and try to add and remove.
cases.expected: Both inert.
cases.oracle: Controls disabled; count unchanged.

cases.title: PR quantities can be reduced and reconcile back
cases.why: Buyers routinely source part of a requisition; the remainder must return to the PR.
cases.setup: A PR line item of 100.
cases.steps: Reduce to 60 on the event. Publish. Open the PR.
cases.expected: The PR shows 60 in progress and 40 still open.
cases.oracle: PR in-progress quantity = 60. `update_quantity_of_purchase_request_items` is the mechanism.

cases.title: A quantity above the PR's is refused
cases.why: Sourcing more than was requisitioned is an approval bypass.
cases.setup: A PR line item of 100.
cases.steps: Set 150 on the event.
cases.expected: Refused with a readable message.
cases.oracle: Refusal; the PR is unchanged.

cases.title: A dormant-locked PR line item blocks creation before anything is written
cases.why: It has a dedicated error shape (not the generic `render_error_json`), and the guard runs before any write — so a partial event must never appear.
cases.setup: A PR whose line item is dormant-locked.
cases.steps: Try to create an event from it.
cases.expected: Refused with the dormant-PR message; no draft created.
cases.oracle: Zero drafts for that PR afterwards. Pairs with API-EG-006.

cases.title: A PR-created event cannot be cloned
cases.why: Already stated as UI-PUB-022; here it is reached from the PR side, which is how a buyer actually meets it.
cases.setup: A published PR-created event.
cases.steps: Try to clone.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Message shown.

cases.title: Multiple PRs merged into one event keep their PR numbers per row
cases.why: The PR-number column is how the buyer proves which requisition a row served.
cases.setup: Two approved PRs.
cases.steps: Create one event from both.
cases.expected: Every line item shows its originating PR number.
cases.oracle: Each row's `pr_number` matches its source PR.

cases.title: Awarding a PR-created event writes back to the PR
cases.why: It closes the intake loop; without it the PR stays open forever.
cases.setup: A PR-created event, awarded.
cases.steps: Complete the award. Open the PR.
cases.expected: The PR reflects the awarded quantity and vendor.
cases.oracle: PR state and awarded quantity match the proposal.

cases.title: Withdrawing a PR-created event returns the quantity to the PR
cases.why: Otherwise a withdrawn event permanently consumes the requisition.
cases.setup: A published PR-created event.
cases.steps: Withdraw it. Open the PR.
cases.expected: The in-progress quantity returns to open.
cases.oracle: PR open quantity is back to its pre-event value.

cases.title: A PR-created event's line item cannot be deleted below one
cases.why: Combines the PR constraint with the 711 rule; the message must be the readable one, not a raw code.
cases.setup: A PR-created event with one line item.
cases.steps: Try to delete it.
cases.expected: Refused with "You cannot delete this line item from the project".
cases.oracle: Message shown; item remains.

cases.title: A single-stage RFQ publishes
cases.why: The most reliable event in the product and the seed for §15 and §16.
cases.setup: Buyer with trade create; single-stage entry.
cases.steps: Create → configure `eventType: rfq`, `awarding: lot` → title → Buy template → fill the first line item → add a participant → Publish.
cases.expected: Lands on `/project/:id/details` with the event Live.
cases.oracle: A real project id in the URL; no error toast.

cases.title: A single-stage RFP publishes
cases.why: The classic path has its own RFP shape, distinct from eRFX's technical stage.
cases.steps: As UI-SS-001 with `eventType: rfp`.
cases.expected: Publishes.
cases.oracle: Project id; the event type reads RFP.

cases.title: A single-stage auction publishes with each sub-type
cases.why: Rank, price and traffic light are all selectable here, and the sub-type section only renders after the event type is chosen — a timing trap.
cases.steps: For each of rank / price / traffic light: configure and publish.
cases.expected: All three publish with the chosen sub-type.
cases.oracle: Sub-type on the live event matches; wait for the conditional section to render before selecting.

cases.title: The configuration drawer renders awarding only after event type
cases.why: Selecting awarding before the type finds nothing and the run reports a missing control.
cases.setup: A fresh single-stage create.
cases.steps: Open the drawer and observe which sections exist before and after choosing a type.
cases.expected: Sub-type and awarding appear only after the type is chosen.
cases.oracle: Options absent before, present after.

cases.title: Awarding "entire lot to a single vendor" is honoured downstream
cases.why: It constrains the awarding grid, so a mismatch surfaces only at award time.
cases.steps: Publish lot-based; reach the awarding screen.
cases.expected: The grid allows one winner for the whole lot.
cases.oracle: Awarding mode reads lot at both ends.

cases.title: Awarding "partially award to multiple vendors" is honoured downstream
cases.why: The other mode, and the one the two-competing-bids journey needs.
cases.steps: Publish line-item based; reach the awarding screen.
cases.expected: Per-line allocation across vendors.
cases.oracle: Awarding mode reads line_item at both ends.

cases.title: Line items are the template's sheet rows
cases.why: It is the structural difference from eRFX, and the reason the eRFX line-item helper does not work here.
cases.setup: A single-stage create with a Buy template.
cases.steps: Fill the first row's product, variant, quantity, delivery and price cells.
cases.expected: One line item exists, defined by that row.
cases.oracle: The row is complete and the event publishes with one item.

cases.title: Adding a second sheet row adds a second line item
cases.why: Multi-line classic events behave differently from eRFX's shared project items.
cases.steps: Add a second row and publish.
cases.expected: Two line items on the live event.
cases.oracle: Line-item count = 2.

cases.title: Publishing with an incomplete row is refused
cases.why: The sheet is the line items here, so a half row is a half event.
cases.steps: Leave the delivery location blank and publish.
cases.expected: Refused with a readable message.
cases.oracle: Publish blocked; no 500.

cases.title: "Invite whole audience" is the fallback when a named vendor is not found
cases.why: It is what keeps the bid journey alive on a tenant where the named test vendor is not in the searchable list — but it must be reported, because the run is then bidding as *someone*, not as the intended vendor.
cases.setup: A vendor search term that matches nothing.
cases.steps: Search, fail, fall back to inviting the audience, publish.
cases.expected: The event publishes with a non-zero audience.
cases.oracle: Audience count > 0 **and** a log line saying the named vendor was not matched. Never assert the specific vendor is on the event after this fallback.

cases.title: Scheduling a single-stage event for later works
cases.why: It was thought broken for a long time; the real cause was that the Schedule control is disabled until a line item exists ("Please choose a template and add a product").
cases.setup: A single-stage create with a template and one line item.
cases.steps: Open Schedule Event, set start/end and evaluation duration, Save Schedule.
cases.expected: The drawer opens and the schedule persists.
cases.oracle: Reopened drawer shows the saved window.

cases.title: A classic event's detail page exposes the same lifecycle controls
cases.why: §15 to §17 navigate from here; if the tabs differ, the later cases need a different path.
cases.setup: A published single-stage event.
cases.steps: Read the tab strip and the Settings menu.
cases.expected: Participants, bids/comparison, Master QCS and Settings are reachable.
cases.oracle: Each entry point resolves.

cases.title: A single-stage event is unaffected by eRFX-only gates
cases.why: It is why this path survived the activation regression, and it is worth an explicit assertion so the isolation is not accidental.
cases.setup: A tenant where eRFX publish is failing.
cases.steps: Publish a single-stage event.
cases.expected: Succeeds.
cases.oracle: Publish succeeds while the eRFX path fails — report both in one run so the contrast is visible.

cases.title: Stage tabs do not appear on a classic tenant
cases.why: The clearest structural assertion that the right screen is under test — the "wrong screen" mistake is the most expensive one in this catalog.
cases.setup: A tenant with `rfx_project_enabled` off.
cases.steps: Open the create screen.
cases.expected: No stage tab strip, no `+` stage control anywhere.
cases.oracle: Zero elements matching the tab strip.

cases.title: An invited vendor sees the event in their Live list
cases.why: If the invitation does not arrive at the portal, nothing else in this section can run, and the cause is on the buyer's side.
cases.setup: A live event with this vendor's company invited by name.
cases.steps: Log in to the portal. Open the events list. Search the event title.
cases.expected: The event is listed under Live with its ref id.
cases.oracle: One matching card; fail loudly rather than falling back to "the first Live event" for any case that asserts something about *this* event.

cases.title: An uninvited vendor does not see the event
cases.why: It is the first half of the isolation promise (PRD §7.2) and it is cheap to check.
cases.setup: A live event; a vendor not on its audience.
cases.steps: Search for the title in that vendor's portal.
cases.expected: No result; direct URL access is refused.
cases.oracle: Zero cards; a direct navigation lands on a refusal, not the event.

cases.title: Opening the event lands on Event Overview
cases.why: It is the tab a test must move *off* of. Filling "the sheet" on the overview finds no cells and reports a missing bid form.
cases.setup: An invited vendor on a live event.
cases.steps: Open the event card.
cases.expected: Event Overview, with the event's details and a stage tab beside it.
cases.oracle: The overview is active; at least one other tab exists.

cases.title: The stage tab exposes the bid sheet
cases.why: The actual entry to bidding.
cases.steps: Switch to the stage tab. Press "Add bid"/"Place bid" if the build shows one.
cases.expected: The bid sheet renders with the buyer's line items and editable price cells.
cases.oracle: At least one non-disabled price cell exists.

cases.title: The vendor sees the buyer's line items, quantities and locations
cases.why: The vendor prices against them; a wrong quantity is a wrong bid.
cases.setup: A live event with two line items of known quantities.
cases.steps: Read the sheet.
cases.expected: Both items, with the buyer's quantities, units and delivery locations.
cases.oracle: Row-by-row comparison against the buyer's event.

cases.title: The vendor fills price cells and the total computes
cases.why: The total is what the buyer compares, and it is derived — a wrong derivation is invisible to both sides.
cases.setup: A bid sheet with a quantity of 10 and a price cell.
cases.steps: Enter 100.
cases.expected: Total = 1000 (plus GST if the template has it, per its rule).
cases.oracle: Rendered total equals the expected arithmetic.

cases.title: Every price cell on a multi-line sheet is filled
cases.why: Submitting with one row priced can be *allowed* while being an incomplete bid. A test that fills only the first row can pass while creating a bid the buyer cannot use.
cases.setup: A 3-line event.
cases.steps: Fill all three price cells. Submit.
cases.expected: All three prices are on the submitted bid.
cases.oracle: Count the cells filled and assert it equals the row count; then check the buyer's comparison shows three prices.

cases.title: Submitting the bid confirms it
cases.why: The core acceptance criterion of PRD §3.4.
cases.steps: Press Submit and confirm if a modal appears.
cases.expected: A success state — the bid is shown as submitted with its values.
cases.oracle: The portal shows the bid as submitted; the buyer's bid count rises by one. Assert both sides, not just the portal's toast.

cases.title: Submitting an empty bid is refused
cases.why: An empty bid would count as participation without a price.
cases.steps: Open the sheet and press Submit with nothing entered.
cases.expected: Refused — the control is disabled or the attempt is rejected with a message.
cases.oracle: No bid appears on the buyer's side.

cases.title: A negative price is refused
cases.why: The backend has a dedicated refusal ("Please enter a valid price", 106) and the portal should not need it.
cases.steps: Enter `-100`. Submit.
cases.expected: Refused with a readable message.
cases.oracle: No bid created; message shown.

cases.title: Zero as a price is either refused or accepted deliberately
cases.why: Free-of-charge lines are real in some categories; whichever the product allows, it must be consistent and visible to the buyer.
cases.steps: Enter `0` and submit.
cases.expected: Consistent behaviour, stated on screen.
cases.oracle: If accepted, the buyer's comparison shows 0 rather than blank.

cases.title: Text in a price cell is refused, not coerced
cases.why: A coerced `0` is a winning bid.
cases.steps: Type `abc` into a price cell.
cases.expected: Refused or cleared with a message; never stored as 0.
cases.oracle: No bid with price 0 created.

cases.title: A negative quantity in the vendor's quantity column is refused
cases.why: Separate refusal from price ("Quantity must be greater than zero", 35).
cases.steps: Enter `-1` as the offered quantity.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Offering more than the requested quantity is refused
cases.why: The backend refuses it ("Quantity should be less than requested quantity", 511) and a vendor over-offering distorts the comparison.
cases.setup: A line item requesting 10.
cases.steps: Offer 15.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: No bid, or the bid capped and the vendor told.

cases.title: Offering in a different unit is refused
cases.why: "Quantity should be in same unit as requested" (512) — a unit mismatch makes every price incomparable.
cases.steps: Change the unit on the offer.
cases.expected: Refused, or the unit is not editable at all.
cases.oracle: The submitted bid's unit equals the requested unit.

cases.title: A negative GST is refused
cases.why: Its own refusal path ("Please enter valid GST", 107).
cases.steps: Enter a negative GST.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A discount above 100% is refused
cases.why: "Please enter a valid discount" (369) — above 100% inverts the price.
cases.setup: gate: trade credit / discount column present.
cases.steps: Enter 150%.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Bidding before the window opens is refused
cases.why: An Upcoming event must not accept bids; the product says "Kindly wait for the auction to start".
cases.setup: An Upcoming event with this vendor invited.
cases.steps: Open it and try to bid.
cases.expected: Cells are not editable, or submission is refused with that message.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Bidding after the window closes is refused
cases.why: The clearest integrity rule in the product: "Order not active" (33). A late bid that lands is a fairness failure, not a UI bug.
cases.setup: A closed event with this vendor invited.
cases.steps: Open it and try to bid.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Bid count on the buyer's side unchanged.

cases.title: Bidding on a withdrawn event is refused
cases.why: Withdrawal must be immediate for vendors, not just cosmetic for the buyer.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event.
cases.steps: As an invited vendor, attempt a bid.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Revising a bid inside the window replaces the value
cases.why: Revision is normal in an auction, and the *latest* bid is what ranks.
cases.setup: A live event with a submitted bid of 100.
cases.steps: Revise to 90 and submit.
cases.expected: The vendor's current bid is 90; the buyer sees 90 as current with 100 in history.
cases.oracle: Buyer's current price = 90; the revision is visible in the bid history.

cases.title: A second bid without revising is refused as already placed
cases.why: The backend distinguishes "revise" from "create again" and refuses the second create ("You have already placed a bid for this company.", 99 / "A bid has already been placed by your team", 96).
cases.setup: A vendor with an active bid.
cases.steps: Attempt to create a fresh bid rather than revising.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: One active bid remains.

cases.title: Another user from the same vendor company cannot bid twice
cases.why: "A bid has already been placed by your team" — the check is at company level, which is the level that matters commercially.
cases.setup: Two users on the same vendor company; one has bid.
cases.steps: As the second user, try to bid.
cases.expected: Refused, with the existing bid visible instead.
cases.oracle: Still one bid for that company.

cases.title: Bidding after revoking a previous bid is refused
cases.why: A dedicated rule ("You cannot place a bid after revoking the previous one", 370) that is easy to violate by accident.
cases.setup: A vendor who revoked their bid.
cases.steps: Try to bid again.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: No new bid.

cases.title: A vendor cannot see another vendor's price
cases.why: PRD §7.2 in the plainest possible form. This is the case you would keep if you could keep only one from this section.
cases.setup: A live event with bids from vendor A (100) and vendor B (90).
cases.steps: As A, inspect every screen the portal offers — sheet, overview, indicators, any comparison.
cases.expected: A sees their own 100 and never B's 90. Rank or a colour is acceptable; a competitor's number is not.
cases.oracle: Scan the rendered page text and the network responses the portal receives for B's price. Checking only the visible DOM is not enough — a price present in the payload is a leak.

cases.title: Rank feedback is shown on a rank-based auction
cases.why: It is the only competitive signal the vendor gets, and it is why the strategy exists.
cases.setup: A live rank auction with two bids.
cases.steps: As the trailing vendor, read the indicator.
cases.expected: A rank (e.g. L2), not a price.
cases.oracle: Rank shown; no competitor price anywhere.

cases.title: Best price is shown on a price-based auction, per configuration
cases.why: Here a number *is* shown deliberately, so the isolation rule and this rule must not be confused with one another.
cases.setup: gate: show-best-price. A live price auction with two bids.
cases.steps: As the trailing vendor, read the indicator.
cases.expected: The best price is shown, without attribution to a vendor.
cases.oracle: The number equals the leading bid; no vendor name accompanies it.

cases.title: A vendor answers the technical questionnaire before pricing
cases.why: It is the RFP half of a two-stage event, and the pricing stage should not be reachable until it is done.
cases.setup: A live RFP + RFQ event with this vendor invited.
cases.steps: Open the technical stage. Answer each question. Submit the response.
cases.expected: The response is submitted and the buyer can see it.
cases.oracle: The buyer's view shows a submitted technical response for this vendor.

cases.title: An incomplete technical response is refused
cases.why: A partial questionnaire cannot be evaluated, and evaluators score against completeness.
cases.steps: Leave a required question blank and submit.
cases.expected: Refused, naming the missing question.
cases.oracle: No submitted response; message identifies the gap.

cases.title: Attaching a document to a bid works and the buyer can open it
cases.why: Bid attachments are contractual (certificates, specs) and a broken link is only discovered at award time.
cases.setup: A live event, bid in progress.
cases.steps: Attach a PDF and submit.
cases.expected: The buyer sees and can download the attachment.
cases.oracle: The file opens from the buyer's side with the original name.

cases.title: A bid survives a portal reload before submission
cases.why: A 40-row sheet lost to a refresh is the vendor's worst experience, and drafts exist to prevent it.
cases.setup: A partially filled bid sheet.
cases.steps: Reload the portal and reopen the event.
cases.expected: Either the draft values are restored, or the vendor is warned before leaving. Not silently emptied.
cases.oracle: Values restored, or a warning was shown.

cases.title: Two vendors bidding on one event produce two competing bids
cases.why: Everything in §17 needs more than one bid to award between, and a journey that accidentally bids twice as the *same* vendor produces one bid while claiming two — a test asserting "two bids" then passes on a broken fixture.
cases.setup: A live event with two distinct vendor companies invited.
cases.steps: As vendor A, bid 100. As vendor B, bid 90.
cases.expected: Two bids from two different companies.
cases.oracle: The buyer's comparison lists two distinct vendor names — assert the *names differ*, not just that the count is 2.

cases.title: The Participants tab of a published event offers Add Bid per vendor
cases.why: It is the entry point, and it lives on a *stage* tab, not the project tab — selecting a stage navigates, so the list arrives with a new page.
cases.setup: A published, live event with invited vendors.
cases.steps: Open the event. Select the stage tab. Open Participants.
cases.expected: The vendor list renders with an Add Bid control on the eligible rows.
cases.oracle: Reaching the list is the success condition — **not** finding an Add Bid control. The list is paginated and only eligible vendors show the control, so a single-vendor event shows a first page of other companies with none. Demanding the control here reports "surrogate bidding is unavailable" when the vendor is simply on another page.

cases.title: A named vendor is found by searching the participant list
cases.why: With 154 vendors, the wanted one is almost never on page one, and a surrogate bid placed for the wrong vendor is worse than none.
cases.setup: A live event with a known vendor on its audience.
cases.steps: Type the vendor's name into the participant search. Wait for the list to narrow.
cases.expected: That vendor's row is visible with its Add Bid control.
cases.oracle: Narrow the list *before* looking for the control; assert the chosen row's text contains the vendor name. Read the name from the row (the `rowItem` ancestor), not from the button's wrapper — the wrapper says only "Add Bid", which makes every vendor look identical and sends every match to the first row.

cases.title: The Add Bid drawer opens with that vendor's sheet
cases.why: The drawer is per-vendor; opening the wrong one attributes the bid to the wrong company.
cases.steps: Click Add Bid on the chosen row.
cases.expected: A drawer with the event's line items and the vendor's name on it.
cases.oracle: Drawer identified by containing the submit control; the vendor name in the drawer matches the row.

cases.title: Submit is disabled until a price is entered
cases.why: It is the product's own guard against an empty surrogate bid, and it doubles as the oracle for "did my values register in the sheet's state".
cases.setup: The drawer open, nothing entered.
cases.steps: Read the submit control.
cases.expected: Disabled.
cases.oracle: Disabled with nothing entered; enabled after one price. If it stays disabled after prices are typed, report exactly that — the values did not register — rather than clicking blindly and reporting "nothing happened".

cases.title: A surrogate bid is submitted and attributed to the vendor
cases.why: The core of PRD §3.4's second half.
cases.steps: Fill every price cell. Submit. Confirm if a modal appears.
cases.expected: The bid is recorded against that vendor, marked as buyer-added.
cases.oracle: The comparison shows a bid for that vendor at that price, flagged surrogate; no error toast after submit.
cases.source: P0 · automate · flow "surrogate bidding by vendor name"

cases.title: Every price cell in the drawer is filled, not just the first
cases.why: The drawer reuses the data grid, so one priced row is enough to enable submit while leaving an incomplete bid — the same trap as UI-VBID-007, on the buyer's side.
cases.setup: A multi-line event.
cases.steps: Fill all price cells (and the offered-quantity cells the grid exposes). Submit.
cases.expected: A complete bid across every line.
cases.oracle: Count the filled cells; assert the buyer's comparison shows a price on every line.

cases.title: Two unnamed surrogate bids land on two different vendors
cases.why: Without tracking who was already bid for, two "give me any vendor" surrogate bids both pick the first row — the event ends with one bid while a test asserting two passes.
cases.setup: A live event with at least two eligible vendors.
cases.steps: Place a surrogate bid without naming a vendor, twice.
cases.expected: Two bids from two different companies.
cases.oracle: The two chosen row texts differ; the comparison shows two distinct vendors.

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a draft event
cases.why: A bid on an unpublished event has nothing to bid against.
cases.setup: A draft event.
cases.steps: Look for the participant list and the control.
cases.expected: Not offered.
cases.oracle: Zero Add Bid controls.

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a withdrawn event
cases.why: Withdrawal must close the buyer's path too, not just the vendor's.
cases.setup: A withdrawn event.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: No Add Bid controls.
cases.oracle: Zero controls.

cases.title: Add Bid is offered on an Upcoming event
cases.why: Deliberately wider than the vendor's own window — a buyer can enter a bid received by phone before the event opens.
cases.setup: An Upcoming event.
cases.steps: Open Participants and place a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Offered and accepted.
cases.oracle: Bid recorded; contrast with UI-VBID-018, where the vendor cannot.

cases.title: After expiry, Add Bid depends on the company's post-expiry setting
cases.why: It is the one setting that changes whether late surrogate bids are possible at all, and it has obvious integrity implications.
cases.setup: Two tenants: post-expiry surrogate bidding on and off. A closed event on each.
cases.steps: Open Participants on each.
cases.expected: Offered where the setting is on, absent where it is off.
cases.oracle: Control presence flips with the setting; where absent, a crafted attempt is refused with "Order not active".

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a knockout auction
cases.why: Knockout runs on automated offers; a manual surrogate bid has no meaning in it.
cases.setup: A live knockout auction.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: No Add Bid drawer.
cases.oracle: Zero controls.

cases.title: Add Bid is absent on a dutch auction
cases.why: Same reasoning, different strategy.
cases.setup: A live dutch auction.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: No Add Bid drawer.
cases.oracle: Zero controls.

cases.title: A technical stage offers Add Technical Bid, not Add Bid
cases.why: They are different controls with different payloads; conflating them makes a technical surrogate response look impossible.
cases.setup: A live RFP stage.
cases.steps: Open Participants.
cases.expected: A technical-bid control, no price drawer.
cases.oracle: The technical control exists; the price drawer does not.

cases.title: A surrogate technical response can be entered for a vendor
cases.why: It is the technical half of surrogate bidding, and the API has a dedicated endpoint for it.
cases.setup: A live RFP stage with an invited vendor.
cases.steps: Add a technical bid for that vendor: answer both the global and the line-item forms, submit.
cases.expected: Submitted and attributed to the vendor.
cases.oracle: The buyer sees a submitted technical response for that vendor, marked surrogate. Pairs with API-SUR-002.

cases.title: Surrogate bidding is refused when the company forbids it
cases.why: `is_buyer_not_allowed_to_add_surrogate_bid` exists precisely so some organisations can bar it, and honouring it is a compliance matter.
cases.setup: An event whose config forbids buyer surrogate bids.
cases.steps: Attempt a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Refused ("You are not allowed to use this functionality", 10).
cases.oracle: No bid created; the control is absent or the attempt refused.

cases.title: Only a valid surrogate bidder may place one
cases.why: The gate is super-admin, a member of a valid bidding team, or the event's own creator. Anyone else placing bids for vendors is a serious problem.
cases.setup: A buyer who is none of those three, on an event they can otherwise see.
cases.steps: Attempt a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Refused (165).
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: A surrogate bid for a vendor who already bid is refused by default
cases.why: Overwriting a vendor's own bid is the most damaging thing this feature could do; by default it is refused (99) and only a specific config allows it.
cases.setup: A vendor who has submitted their own bid, on a tenant without `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid`.
cases.steps: Attempt a surrogate bid for them.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: The vendor's own bid is unchanged.

cases.title: Where the config allows it, a later surrogate bid revises rather than duplicates
cases.why: With `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid` on, the product *revises* the existing surrogate bid. Creating a second one instead would double-count the vendor in the comparison.
cases.setup: gate: `allowed_surrogate_bid_even_after_bid`. A vendor with an existing surrogate bid.
cases.steps: Place another surrogate bid for them at a new price.
cases.expected: One bid, at the new price, with the old value in history.
cases.oracle: Bid count for that vendor is still 1; the current price is the new one.

cases.title: A surrogate bid may require approval before it counts
cases.why: On tenants with a surrogate-bid approval flow, the bid is *requested*, not active — and a test asserting an immediate active bid fails there forever.
cases.setup: gate: surrogate-bid approval configured.
cases.steps: Place a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: It enters an approval-pending state and an approver has a task.
cases.oracle: Bid status is approval-requested; the approver's task list contains it.

cases.title: Reading the surrogate approval flows needs approval-read permission
cases.why: It is the one genuinely gated method on an otherwise open bid policy, which makes it easy to lose.
cases.setup: A buyer without approval-flow read permission.
cases.steps: Trigger the surrogate approval-flow lookup.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Refusal rather than an empty list — an empty list would look like "no approval needed" and let the bid through. Pairs with API-SUR-011.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is visibly marked as buyer-entered
cases.why: At award time it matters enormously whether a price came from the vendor or from the buyer's phone call. If it is not labelled, the audit trail is gone.
cases.setup: An event with one vendor bid and one surrogate bid.
cases.steps: Read the buyer's comparison.
cases.expected: The surrogate bid is labelled as such; the vendor's own is not.
cases.oracle: The label is present on exactly one of the two.

cases.title: A surrogate bid is refused with a negative or absent price
cases.why: Same validation as a vendor's bid; the surrogate path must not be the lenient one.
cases.steps: Enter a negative price, then clear the cell entirely, and try to submit each time.
cases.expected: Refused both times.
cases.oracle: Submit stays disabled for the empty case; a message for the negative.

cases.title: A surrogate bid appears to the vendor as their own bid
cases.why: If the vendor cannot see it, they may bid again and the two disagree; if they can, they can query it. Either way, the state must be honest.
cases.setup: An event with a surrogate bid placed for a vendor.
cases.steps: As that vendor, open the event.
cases.expected: The bid is visible with its price, and the product is clear about who entered it.
cases.oracle: The vendor's portal shows a bid at that price.

cases.title: Master QCS is reachable on a closed event with bids
cases.why: It is the door to awarding; if it does not open, nothing else here runs.
cases.setup: A published event with at least one submitted bid.
cases.steps: Open the event → Master QCS tab.
cases.expected: The comparison grid renders with the line items and the bidding vendors.
cases.oracle: The grid is present and lists the expected vendor(s).

cases.title: The comparison shows every bid, per line item, with totals
cases.why: It is the decision surface. A missing or misattributed bid here produces a wrong award.
cases.setup: An event with two vendors' bids at known prices.
cases.steps: Read the grid.
cases.expected: Both vendors, both prices, correct per-line and total amounts.
cases.oracle: Compare every rendered price against the fixture; assert the vendor names are the real ones and not placeholders.

cases.title: Start Awarding enters the awarding flow
cases.why: The first of the two entry controls.
cases.setup: An event with bids and no proposal yet.
cases.steps: Press Start Awarding.
cases.expected: The awarding screen opens for this event.
cases.oracle: URL moves to the awarding route with the event's id.

cases.title: Bid Selection Proposal re-enters the flow once a draft proposal exists
cases.why: Without this, awarding appears to work once per event and then vanish.
cases.setup: An event with a draft proposal.
cases.steps: Return to Master QCS and read the entry control.
cases.expected: "Bid Selection Proposal" with a Draft tag, and it re-enters the flow.
cases.oracle: The second control exists and navigates; the first is absent.

cases.title: A disabled awarding control explains itself
cases.why: Awarding is gated by `is_awarding_allowed` and the button carries a tooltip saying why — a live event, a stage still in draft, or a superseded version. That reason is worth reporting instead of discovering as a dead click.
cases.setup: A live event whose bidding is still open.
cases.steps: Hover the awarding control.
cases.expected: Disabled, with a tooltip naming the reason.
cases.oracle: Report the tooltip text; do not click through.

cases.title: Awarding is blocked while a selected or requested proposal exists
cases.why: Two live proposals on one event would award it twice.
cases.setup: An event with a submitted (requested) proposal.
cases.steps: Try to start a new award.
cases.expected: Blocked, with the existing proposal offered instead.
cases.oracle: No second proposal is created. Pairs with API-AWD-005.

cases.title: Awarding is blocked while this user holds a draft proposal
cases.why: The gate is per-user for drafts, which is subtly different from the previous case.
cases.setup: The same buyer with a draft proposal on the event.
cases.steps: Try to start a fresh award.
cases.expected: Blocked; the draft is offered.
cases.oracle: Proposal count unchanged.

cases.title: Allocating a line item to a vendor moves the item counter
cases.why: It is one of the two counters, and it is the one that says *what* is being awarded.
cases.setup: The awarding grid with two line items.
cases.steps: Allocate one line item to a vendor.
cases.expected: "Tot. selected line items" reads 1/2.
cases.oracle: Read the app's own counter — it is a more honest oracle than inferring which checkbox belongs to which vendor from the DOM.

cases.title: Awarding a vendor moves the vendor counter
cases.why: It is the counter the Create Proposal validation actually checks, and the one that was mistaken for an unrelated toggle.
cases.steps: Tick the control that awards the vendor.
cases.expected: "Awarded Vendors" rises to 1.
cases.oracle: Both counters must be non-zero before Create Proposal; assert each separately so a failure says which one is missing.

cases.title: Create Proposal is refused with no vendor awarded
cases.why: It is the exact failure the two-counter confusion produced: "Please award for at least one Vendor".
cases.setup: Line items allocated but no vendor awarded.
cases.steps: Press Create Proposal.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: Message shown; no proposal created.

cases.title: Create Proposal produces a draft proposal
cases.why: Creation and submission are deliberately separate — which is why the Master QCS control changes — and a draft proposal is not an awarded event.
cases.steps: Allocate, award, Create Proposal.
cases.expected: A draft proposal exists with the allocation on it.
cases.oracle: Proposal exists in draft with the expected vendor and line items. A missing submit control must be reported, not treated as success.

cases.title: Submitting the proposal sends it into the approval workflow
cases.why: PRD §3.5 — the award goes through a proposal *and* an approval workflow. Submission is the point of no return.
cases.steps: Submit the draft proposal.
cases.expected: Status moves to requested; approvers have tasks.
cases.oracle: Proposal status requested; approver task exists.

cases.title: An approver approves and the award completes
cases.why: It is the last step of the whole catalog and the one that changes commercial reality.
cases.setup: A submitted proposal and its approver.
cases.steps: As the approver, open the task and approve.
cases.expected: The proposal is selected; the event shows as awarded to that vendor.
cases.oracle: Event state awarded; the awarded vendor and quantity match the allocation.

cases.title: A rejected proposal returns the event to awardable
cases.why: Otherwise a rejection deadlocks the event.
cases.setup: A submitted proposal.
cases.steps: As the approver, reject with remarks.
cases.expected: The event can be awarded again; the rejection and remarks are recorded.
cases.oracle: Awarding controls re-enable; the rejection is in the history.

cases.title: Discarding a draft proposal re-enables awarding
cases.why: It is the escape hatch from UI-AWD-007, and it must actually clear the gate.
cases.setup: A draft proposal.
cases.steps: Discard it.
cases.expected: Awarding is available again.
cases.oracle: The Start Awarding control returns.

cases.title: Partial awarding splits one line item across vendors
cases.why: It is the whole reason line-item awarding mode exists, and the quantities must add up.
cases.setup: A line-item-awarding event with a quantity of 100 and two bids.
cases.steps: Award 60 to A and 40 to B.
cases.expected: Both allocations recorded; total awarded = 100.
cases.oracle: Sum of awarded quantities equals the requested quantity; neither vendor exceeds their offered quantity.

cases.title: Awarding more than the requested quantity is refused
cases.why: Over-awarding creates a commitment the requisition never covered.
cases.setup: A quantity of 100.
cases.steps: Try to award 60 + 60.
cases.expected: Refused with a readable message.
cases.oracle: No proposal with 120 awarded.

cases.title: Awarding the whole lot on a partial-lot RFQ is refused
cases.why: The backend refuses it in words ("You cannot award entire lot when RFQ was done for partial lot.", 503) and the reason is genuinely non-obvious.
cases.setup: An RFQ run as partial lot.
cases.steps: Try to award the entire lot to one vendor.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: Message shown; no proposal.

cases.title: Closing the bid to select a winner is refused outside the allowed window
cases.why: `close_bid` has its own timing gate ("Unable to close the order at this time. Please wait for the bidding to end", 9), and closing early would cut off bids that were still permitted.
cases.setup: A live event still inside its bidding window.
cases.steps: Attempt to close the bid and select a winner.
cases.expected: Refused with that message.
cases.oracle: The event stays live; no winner is set.

cases.title: The awarding report downloads and matches the screen
cases.why: The report is what leaves the building — it goes to finance and to the vendor. A mismatch with the screen is the most consequential inconsistency in the module.
cases.setup: An awarded event.
cases.steps: Download the awarding sheet.
cases.expected: A file whose vendors, line items, quantities and prices match the grid.
cases.oracle: Parse the file and compare the numbers cell by cell against the rendered grid.

cases.title: A vendor cannot open an event they were not invited to
cases.why: Direct-URL access is the first thing anyone tries.
cases.setup: An event's URL and an uninvited vendor.
cases.steps: Navigate directly.
cases.expected: Refused, not rendered.
cases.oracle: The event's title and prices are absent from the response.

cases.title: A vendor with no visible stage cannot view the event at all
cases.why: Read permission alone is not enough — the policy also requires at least one visible stage, which is a rule people forget exists.
cases.setup: A vendor on the company's platform but not on any stage's audience.
cases.steps: Attempt to open the event.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: Authorization failure rather than an empty event page. Pairs with API-PERM-001.

cases.title: A buyer from another company cannot see the event
cases.why: Cross-tenant isolation, the highest-stakes boundary in the system.
cases.setup: Two companies; an event in company A.
cases.steps: As a buyer in company B, search for and navigate to it.
cases.expected: Not found; direct access refused.
cases.oracle: Zero rows and a refusal.

cases.title: A buyer without trade-create permission cannot create or publish
cases.why: Permissions are team-based here, so a user can look like a buyer and not be one.
cases.setup: A user whose teams grant read but not create on `trade`.
cases.steps: Try to reach the create screen and publish.
cases.expected: Refused or unavailable.
cases.oracle: No event created.

cases.title: A user without sourcing-events access cannot create a stage
cases.why: `has_access_for_sourcing_events?` is a second, independent gate on stage creation; passing the first and failing this one is a real configuration.
cases.setup: A user with trade-create but without sourcing-events access.
cases.steps: Attempt to create a stage.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No stage created. Pairs with API-PERM-004.

cases.title: A planner cannot clone an event
cases.why: A specific policy carve-out that would otherwise pass silently because cloning needs only create permission.
cases.setup: A planner with create permission.
cases.steps: Try to clone an active event.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No clone created.

cases.title: Vendor masking removes the Audience tab
cases.why: gate: `isVendorMaskingEnabled`. Masking exists so a buyer's team cannot see who is bidding; leaving the tab in defeats it entirely.
cases.setup: gate: `isVendorMaskingEnabled`.
cases.steps: Open a published event's tabs.
cases.expected: No Audience tab.
cases.oracle: Tab absent from the list.

cases.title: Vendor masking hides vendor identities in the comparison
cases.why: The tab being gone is worthless if the names appear on the grid.
cases.setup: gate: `isVendorMaskingEnabled`. An event with two bids.
cases.steps: Open Master QCS.
cases.expected: Vendors appear as anonymised labels, not company names.
cases.oracle: No real vendor name in the rendered grid **or** in the payload behind it.

cases.title: An evaluator sees the technical response and not the prices
cases.why: The separation of technical and commercial evaluation is the point of a two-stage event.
cases.setup: An RFP + RFQ event with a submitted technical response and a bid.
cases.steps: As the evaluator, open the response.
cases.expected: Questionnaire answers visible; prices not.
cases.oracle: No bid price in the evaluator's view or its payload.

cases.title: A vendor cannot reach the buyer console
cases.why: Two applications, one identity provider — the boundary must hold.
cases.setup: Vendor credentials.
cases.steps: Try to log into the buyer console.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No authenticated buyer session.

cases.title: A buyer cannot place a bid as their own company
cases.why: "Cannot place bid on trade by your own company" (165) — otherwise a buyer could bid against their own event.
cases.setup: A buyer on their own event.
cases.steps: Attempt to bid as the buying company.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bid created.

cases.title: Feedback on a bid is restricted to the order's team or a super admin
cases.why: A narrow gate on an otherwise open bid policy, so it is easy to lose in a refactor.
cases.setup: A buyer not on the order's team and not a super admin.
cases.steps: Attempt to add feedback on a bid.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No feedback recorded. Pairs with API-PERM-011.

cases.title: Uploading a bid Excel needs view access to the event
cases.why: It is a bulk write path, and bulk write paths with weak authorization are the worst kind.
cases.setup: A user without view access to the event.
cases.steps: Attempt the upload.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No bids created.

cases.title: Session expiry mid-journey is handled, not crashed into
cases.why: A long bidding session outlives a token, and the vendor must be told rather than losing a filled sheet to a silent failure.
cases.setup: A filled bid sheet and an expired session.
cases.steps: Submit.
cases.expected: A re-authentication prompt or a clear message; the entered values are not lost without warning.
cases.oracle: A readable message rather than a blank screen or a swallowed error.

cases.title: Every required field on the create screen is enforced
cases.why: It is the requirement stated most broadly in the PRD, so it needs a systematic case rather than one per field.
cases.setup: A create screen.
cases.steps: Attempt publish with each required field blank in turn — title, template, line items, schedule, participants.
cases.expected: Each is refused with a message naming the field. No partial event.
cases.oracle: For each: publish blocked, message present, and zero events created.

cases.title: A whitespace-only title is treated as blank
cases.why: It is the standard way past a presence check.
cases.steps: Title `" "`. Publish.
cases.expected: Refused as missing.
cases.oracle: Publish blocked.

cases.title: HTML in a title is escaped, not rendered
cases.why: Stored XSS in an event title would reach every invited vendor.
cases.steps: Title ``. Publish. View the list, the detail page and the vendor's portal.
cases.expected: The text renders literally; no script executes anywhere.
cases.oracle: No dialog/console error; the DOM contains escaped text, not an element.

cases.title: A script payload in a line-item or clause field is escaped
cases.why: Titles are the obvious field; clauses and item descriptions reach vendors too.
cases.steps: Put the same payload in a T&C clause and an item description. Publish. View as the vendor.
cases.expected: Escaped everywhere.
cases.oracle: No execution in either view.

cases.title: SQL-ish input is handled as text
cases.why: `'; DROP TABLE` in a search box is the cheapest smoke test for a whole class of failure.
cases.steps: Search the events list and the participant list for `'; DROP TABLE event_groups; --`.
cases.expected: Zero or literal matches; no error.
cases.oracle: A normal empty-result state; no 500.

cases.title: A very long string in every text field is bounded politely
cases.why: PRD §6. Unbounded fields become database errors, which become 500s.
cases.steps: Enter 10,000 characters into the title, description and a clause.
cases.expected: Either accepted whole or refused with a stated limit. No 500, no silent truncation.
cases.oracle: Per field: a message, or a value that round-trips exactly.

cases.title: Emoji survive in titles, descriptions and clauses
cases.why: Four-byte characters are where encoding assumptions break.
cases.steps: Use emoji in each. Publish. Read back on the buyer's and vendor's views.
cases.expected: Identical rendering everywhere.
cases.oracle: Byte equality on read-back.

cases.title: Right-to-left and CJK text render without breaking layout
cases.why: Real tenants have them, and a broken grid is unusable rather than merely ugly.
cases.steps: Enter Arabic and Chinese text in a title and a line-item description.
cases.expected: Rendered correctly; the sheet's columns stay aligned.
cases.oracle: No horizontal overflow of the grid container; text matches.

cases.title: Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed consistently
cases.why: `"RFQ "` and `"RFQ"` as two different titles makes search unreliable for everyone.
cases.steps: Publish with `" Event A "`. Search for `"Event A"`.
cases.expected: Found; the stored title is trimmed.
cases.oracle: Search hit and an exact stored value.

cases.title: A number field rejects `e`-notation and thousands separators
cases.why: `1e5` and `1,00,000` both parse to something unexpected somewhere in the stack.
cases.steps: Enter `1e5` and `1,00,000` into a price cell.
cases.expected: Refused or normalised visibly. Not stored as an unrelated number.
cases.oracle: The stored value equals what is displayed.

cases.title: More decimal places than the template allows are rounded visibly
cases.why: Silent rounding of a price changes the bid.
cases.steps: Enter `100.999` where 2 decimals are configured.
cases.expected: Rounded to `101.00` **and** shown that way before submission.
cases.oracle: Displayed and stored values agree.

cases.title: Duplicate product names in master data do not confuse the picker
cases.why: PRD §6 lists duplicate product names; the picker must disambiguate or the buyer adds the wrong item.
cases.setup: Two products with the same name and different codes.
cases.steps: Search for the name in the line-items picker.
cases.expected: Both are offered, distinguishable (code, category or variant).
cases.oracle: Two options with distinguishing text; the chosen one is the one that lands.

cases.title: A duplicate user email is refused when adding a user
cases.why: PRD §6, and duplicated identities break team-based permissions.
cases.setup: An existing user's email.
cases.steps: Create a user with the same email.
cases.expected: Refused with a readable message.
cases.oracle: No second user created.

cases.title: A 10-digit phone number is accepted and stored with a country prefix
cases.why: The PRD states this as an acceptance criterion *and* flags it for verification: the specified rule is "any 10-digit number, prefixed `+91` by default". If the product is stricter or looser, the difference is the finding.
cases.setup: The user-create form.
cases.steps: Enter `9876543210` and save. Then try `1234567890`, `0000000000`, a 9-digit and an 11-digit number.
cases.expected: All 10-digit values accepted and stored as `+91…`; 9- and 11-digit refused.
cases.oracle: Record the exact behaviour per input and compare against the specified rule — this case is expected to produce a finding either way.

cases.title: An invalid email format is refused
cases.why: PRD §5 names email format explicitly, and it is the field most often loosely validated.
cases.steps: Try `a@`, `a@b`, `a b@c.com`, `a@@b.com`.
cases.expected: All refused with a format message.
cases.oracle: No record created for any of them.

cases.title: A malformed request never produces a partial event
cases.why: PRD §5's "no partial record" clause. A half-written event is worse than a refused one because nobody knows it exists.
cases.setup: A crafted create request with a malformed `line_items` (a string, not an array).
cases.steps: Send it.
cases.expected: A 4xx with a readable message; nothing written.
cases.oracle: No event group and no line items created. Pairs with API-VAL-003.

cases.title: Every validation message is readable and names the problem
cases.why: PRD §5's "politely" clause is a real requirement. `Error 712` on screen is a defect even when the refusal is correct.
cases.setup: Any five refusal paths from this catalog.
cases.steps: Trigger each and read the message.
cases.expected: Each is a sentence naming the problem, not a bare code.
cases.oracle: No message consists only of a number; each contains a field or an action.

cases.title: A failed request does not leave the screen in a dead state
cases.why: After the activation regression, the button did nothing and the buyer had no idea why — the absence of feedback was as damaging as the failure.
cases.setup: Any refused publish.
cases.steps: After the refusal, try to correct the problem and publish again.
cases.expected: The screen is still usable; the second attempt works.
cases.oracle: No reload needed to recover; the retry succeeds.

cases.title: The events list stays under the 3-second target as volume grows
cases.why: PRD §7.1, measured rather than assumed.
cases.setup: Tenants with ~10, ~100 and ~1000 events.
cases.steps: Time a cold load of the list on each.
cases.expected: Under ~3s throughout.
cases.oracle: Record the three numbers and trend them; flag regressions rather than asserting a hard threshold on shared infrastructure.

cases.title: The create screen stays responsive with 65 line items
cases.why: The sheet is the heaviest component in the product and the cap is the realistic worst case for a non-BOQ event.
cases.setup: A non-BOQ event at the cap.
cases.steps: Scroll and edit cells at the top and bottom of the sheet.
cases.expected: Edits register without visible lag; no dropped keystrokes.
cases.oracle: Every value entered is present after the pass.

cases.title: A 500-row BOQ sheet renders and can be scrolled
cases.why: PRD §6's large-event case, at the UI layer.
cases.setup: A 500-item BOQ event.
cases.steps: Open the sheet; scroll to the last row.
cases.expected: It renders (virtualised is fine) and the last row is reachable.
cases.oracle: Row 500 is present and correct.

cases.title: Publishing a 500-item event completes within a stated budget
cases.why: A publish that times out client-side while succeeding server-side is the worst outcome: the buyer retries and creates a second event.
cases.setup: A 500-item BOQ event.
cases.steps: Publish and time it.
cases.expected: Completes; the client waits long enough. If it times out, the event must not be duplicated by a retry.
cases.oracle: One event afterwards, whatever the timing; record the duration.

cases.title: A slow network does not double-submit a bid
cases.why: Vendors bid on bad connections at the last minute; a duplicate bid is a real integrity problem.
cases.setup: Throttled network, a live event.
cases.steps: Submit a bid and click again while it is in flight.
cases.expected: One bid.
cases.oracle: Bid count = 1 on the buyer's side.

cases.title: A dropped connection mid-publish leaves a recoverable state
cases.why: PRD §7.3 — a half-finished action must corrupt nothing.
cases.setup: A valid event.
cases.steps: Kill the network during the publish request. Restore it. Reload.
cases.expected: Either published or still a draft; never a broken half-state, and never two events.
cases.oracle: Exactly one event with that title, in a coherent status.

cases.title: The bid countdown agrees with the server's clock
cases.why: A vendor bidding against a fast client clock loses the event through no fault of their own.
cases.setup: A live event near its end.
cases.steps: Compare the rendered countdown with the server's end time.
cases.expected: Within a couple of seconds.
cases.oracle: Difference under a small threshold; a client-clock skew must not shift it.

cases.title: Two buyers editing one draft do not silently overwrite each other
cases.why: The version guard exists for this, and the failure mode is losing a colleague's work without either of them knowing.
cases.setup: One draft, two buyers.
cases.steps: Both edit; both save.
cases.expected: The second save is either merged or refused as stale, with a message.
cases.oracle: No silent loss: after both saves, the surviving state is explainable and the loser was told. Pairs with UI-PUB-011.

cases.title: The console recovers from a backend 5xx without losing the form
cases.why: During the activation regression every publish failed; how the screen behaved then decided whether buyers lost their work as well as their event.
cases.setup: A create screen with a full configuration; force a 5xx on publish.
cases.steps: Publish. Read the screen.
cases.expected: An error is surfaced and every entered value is still there.
cases.oracle: The form retains its values; a message is visible.

cases.title: Accessibility basics on the create and bid screens
cases.why: They are the two screens people spend hours in, and the automation depends on roles and labels to find anything at all — so it is also a testability matter.
cases.setup: The create screen and the vendor bid sheet.
cases.steps: Tab through each; check that every control has an accessible name.
cases.expected: Focus order follows the visual order; no unlabelled interactive control.
cases.oracle: An accessibility scan with zero critical violations on named controls.

cases.title: OTP login returns a usable session for a buyer
cases.why: Every case after this one depends on it, and the two-step generate/verify shape is easy to get wrong.
cases.setup: A buyer phone/email with a known test OTP.
cases.steps: `POST /v1/generate_otp`, then `POST /v1/verify_otp` with the code.
cases.expected: 200 with a session/token the subsequent calls accept.
cases.oracle: A following authenticated read succeeds with the returned credential.

cases.title: A wrong OTP is refused
cases.why: "Invalid OTP" (6) must be a refusal, not a 500, and not a success.
cases.steps: Verify with a wrong code.
cases.expected: 422 with code 6.
cases.oracle: No session issued.

cases.title: The stored session is reused across the suite
cases.why: Re-authenticating per test triples the run and invites OTP rate limits.
cases.setup: A saved auth state.
cases.steps: Run two specs back to back.
cases.expected: Both use the stored session; no second OTP request.
cases.oracle: One auth exchange per run.

cases.title: An expired or absent token is refused everywhere
cases.why: An endpoint that answers unauthenticated is the worst possible finding, and it must be checked on writes as well as reads.
cases.steps: Call `GET /api/event_groups`, `POST /api/event_groups` and `POST /v1/bids` with no credential and with a corrupted one.
cases.expected: All refused.
cases.oracle: Nothing created by the write attempts.

cases.title: The dashboard configuration reports the tenant's real capabilities
cases.why: It is the source the gating decisions read; if it lies, every gated case is decided wrongly.
cases.steps: `GET /v1/dashboard_configuration`.
cases.expected: Flags and module permissions matching the tenant.
cases.oracle: Spot-check three flags against observed endpoint behaviour.

cases.title: A vendor session cannot call buyer endpoints
cases.why: The two apps share an identity layer; the authorization boundary is the only separation.
cases.setup: A vendor session.
cases.steps: Call `POST /api/event_groups`.
cases.expected: Refused.
cases.oracle: No event group created.

cases.title: A user from company B cannot read company A's event
cases.why: Cross-tenant isolation at the API layer, where it actually lives.
cases.setup: An event in company A; a session in company B.
cases.steps: `GET /api/event_groups/:id` for A's event.
cases.expected: Refused (not an empty 200).
cases.oracle: No event payload in the response body.

cases.title: Multi-company users act in exactly one workspace at a time
cases.why: A user attached to several companies is a real configuration, and ambiguity here writes data into the wrong tenant.
cases.setup: gate: multi-company user. A user in two companies.
cases.steps: Select company A, create a draft; select company B, list events.
